lessons.title: The main trigonometrical ratios of the acute angle

objectives.label: Convert degrees, minutes, seconds
objectives.description: Convert angles between degrees, minutes and seconds and decimal degrees, by hand or with the calculator.

objectives.label: Compare sides and ratios
objectives.description: Compare sides of a right angled triangle and ratios of sides to 1 using the symbols >, < or =.

objectives.label: Calculate sin, cos, tan
objectives.description: Calculate sin, cos and tan of an acute angle in a right angled triangle as ratios of the opposite, adjacent and hypotenuse sides, finding a missing side where needed.

objectives.label: Prove ratio relationships
objectives.description: Prove relationships between trigonometrical ratios of acute angles in a right angled triangle.

entries.text: Right-angled triangle with vertices A at top, B at bottom left with right-angle mark, C at bottom right. Hypotenuse AC. Read from figure; verify.

A.why: The right-angled triangle ABC with hypotenuse AC is the figure for comparing sides and ratios to 1.

B.why: Right triangle ABC with hypotenuse AC is the figure for the side-comparison activities.

entries.text: Circular protractor-like ring with two perpendicular axes with arrows, marked in degrees every 10 from 10 to 360 (10, 20, 30 ... 90 at top, 180 left, 270 bottom, 360 right). Read from figure; verify.

A.why: The ring marked in degrees illustrates measuring angles in degrees, the unit being converted.

B.why: Degree-marked circle illustrates measuring angles in degrees, the unit being subdivided.

entries.text: 35 degrees, 24 minutes, 42 seconds is written as $35^\circ 24' 42''$. $35^\circ, 24', 42''$

A.why: It shows how degrees, minutes and seconds are written as 35° 24' 42''.

B.why: Shows how degrees, minutes and seconds are written in symbols.

entries.text: Picture of a scientific calculator, with the degree-minute-second key shown in the text as a button.

A.why: The calculator's degree-minute-second key is used to convert angles by calculator.

B.why: Shows the calculator degree-minute-second key used for converting angle units.

entries.text: Right-angled triangle ABC with right angle at B (marked), A at top, B bottom left, C bottom right. Side AB labelled 'opposite', side BC labelled 'adjacent', side AC labelled 'hypotenuse'.

A.why: The triangle labelled opposite, adjacent and hypotenuse sets up the sides for the ratios sin, cos and tan.

B.why: Labels opposite, adjacent and hypotenuse sides used to define sin, cos and tan.

entries.text: Sine angle is denoted by the symbol sin.

A.why: It names the sine ratio with the symbol sin.

B.why: Names sin as the symbol for the sine ratio of an acute angle.

entries.text: Cosine angle is denoted by the symbol cos.

A.why: It names the cosine ratio with the symbol cos.

B.why: Names cos as the symbol for the cosine ratio of an acute angle.

entries.text: Tangential angle is denoted by the symbol tan.

A.why: It names the tangent ratio with the symbol tan.

B.why: Names tan as the symbol for the tangent ratio of an acute angle.

entries.text: Right triangle ABC with right angle marked at C; A at top right, B at left, C at bottom right; hypotenuse AB = 13 cm, base BC = 12 cm.

A.why: The triangle with AB = 13 cm and BC = 12 cm belongs to the worked example finding a missing side.

B.why: The 13 cm, 12 cm right triangle belongs to the worked example finding a missing side and ratios.

lessons.title: The main trigonometrical ratios of some angles

objectives.label: Ratios of 30°, 60°, 45°
objectives.description: Determine the trigonometric ratios (sin, cos, tan) of the special angles 30°, 60° and 45° from the side ratios of an equilateral triangle and an isosceles right-angled triangle, and state that sin of an angle equals cos of its complementary angle.

objectives.label: Evaluate special-angle expressions
objectives.description: Evaluate and prove expressions involving the ratios of 30°, 45° and 60°, using exact values and the relations sin A = cos of the complementary angle and tan A = sin A / cos A.

objectives.label: Ratios of angles by calculator
objectives.description: Use a calculator to find the trigonometric ratio of a given angle, including angles in degrees, minutes and seconds.

objectives.label: Find angle from its ratio
objectives.description: Find the measure of an angle from its trigonometrical ratio, using the calculator or special-angle values, and apply this to find angles and areas in a triangle.

entries.text: Equilateral triangle ABC with vertex A at top, C bottom left, B bottom right; AD drawn from A to D on CB with a right-angle mark at D.

A.why: Equilateral triangle with altitude AD is used to derive 30° and 60° ratios.

B.why: Equilateral triangle with altitude AD used to derive 30° and 60° ratios.

entries.text: Right triangle ABD with right angle at D; angle at A is 30°, angle at B is 60°; AB = 2 (hypotenuse), BD = 1, AD = √3.

A.why: Right triangle with 30°, 60° and sides 1, √3, 2 gives the special-angle ratios.

B.why: 30°-60° right triangle with sides 1, 2, √3 for deriving ratios.

entries.text: tan 30° = BD/AD = 1/√3 $\tan 30^\circ=\frac{BD}{AD}=\frac{1}{\sqrt3}$

A.why: tan 30° derived from the side ratios of the triangle.

B.why: Gives tan 30° from the equilateral triangle.

entries.text: sin 60° = AD/AB = √3/2 $\sin 60^\circ=\frac{AD}{AB}=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$

A.why: sin 60° derived from the equilateral triangle sides.

B.why: Gives sin 60° from the equilateral triangle.

entries.text: cos 60° = BD/AB = 1/2 and tan 60° = AD/BD = √3 $\cos 60^\circ=\frac{BD}{AB}=\frac12$, $\tan 60^\circ=\frac{AD}{BD}=\sqrt3$

A.why: cos 60° and tan 60° derived from the triangle sides.

B.why: Gives cos 60° and tan 60° from the equilateral triangle.

entries.text: Right triangle ABC with right angle at C (square marker). A at top, B at bottom left, C at bottom right. Legs AC and BC marked equal with tick marks and labelled L each. Hypotenuse AB.

A.why: Isosceles right triangle used to derive the 45° ratios.

B.why: Isosceles right triangle used to derive the ratios of 45°.

entries.text: sin 45° = AC/AB = 1/√2, cos 45° = BC/AB = 1/√2, tan 45° = AC/BC = 1. $\sin 45^\circ=\frac{AC}{AB}=\frac{1}{\sqrt2},\ \cos 45^\circ=\frac{BC}{AB}=\frac{1}{\sqrt2},\ \tan 45^\circ=\frac{AC}{BC}=1$

A.why: sin, cos, tan of 45° from the isosceles right triangle.

B.why: Gives sin, cos, tan of 45° from the isosceles right triangle.

entries.text: Trigonometric ratios of 30°, 60°, 45°; rows Sin, Cos, Tan. m angle \ ratio, 30°, 60°, 45° / Sin, $\frac{1}{2}$, $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ / Cos, $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, $\frac{1}{2}$, $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ / Tan, $\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$, $\sqrt{3}$, 1

A.why: Summarises the ratios of 30°, 60°, 45°.

B.why: Table summarising the ratios of 30°, 60°, 45°.

entries.text: The sine of any angle equals the cosine of the supplementary (complementary) angle of this angle, and vice versa.

A.why: States sin of an angle equals cos of its complementary angle, named in objective 1.

B.why: States that sin of an angle equals cos of its complementary angle.

entries.text: Picture of a scientific calculator beside Example 2; no values readable.

A.why: Calculator picture beside the example on finding ratios by calculator.

B.why: Calculator picture beside Example 2 on finding ratios by calculator.

entries.text: Right-angled triangle (right angle at bottom left, marked with a square); angle 30° at bottom right; vertical side 1; hypotenuse 2; horizontal base $\sqrt{3}$.

A.why: 30° triangle used to find an angle from its ratio using special-angle values.

B.why: 30° right triangle with sides 1, 2, √3 illustrating the special-angle ratios.

entries.text: Calculator key sequence: Start → SHIFT, sin, 0,544639035, =, then the degrees-minutes-seconds key, giving 33°.

A.why: Calculator key sequence using SHIFT sin to find the angle 33°.

B.why: Calculator sequence using SHIFT sin to get the angle from its ratio.

entries.text: Isosceles triangle ABC with apex A, base CB; AB and AC each marked 8 cm; AD drawn perpendicular to CB with D on CB and right angle marked; CD = 6 cm, DB = 6 cm.

A.why: Isosceles triangle figure for the Connecting with Geometry example finding angles and area.

B.why: Figure of the isosceles triangle ABC in the geometry example finding angles and area.

entries.text: Use the calculator as follows: start 1 ÷ 2 × 12 × 8 × sin 41 ° ' '' 24 ° ' '' 35 ° ' '' =

A.why: Calculator steps for the triangle area (1/2 × 12 × 8 × sin angle) in the geometry example.

B.why: Calculator steps for the area of the isosceles triangle, the Connecting with Geometry example.
